Let the sum due be \(A\).  
Present worth \(P=\dfrac{A}{(1.12)^5}\), so true discount:
\[
TD=A-P=A\left(1-\frac1{1.12^5}\right)
\]
Banker’s discount:
\[
BD=A\times 0.12\times 5=0.6A
\]
Given:
\[
270=BD-TD=0.6A-A\left(1-\frac1{1.12^5}\right)
=A\left(\frac1{1.12^5}-0.4\right)
\]
Thus:
\[
BD=0.6A=\frac{0.6\times 270}{\frac1{1.12^5}-0.4}
\]
Since \(1.12^5=1.7623416832\),
\[
\frac1{1.12^5}\approx 0.567426856
\]
\[
BD=\frac{162}{0.567426856-0.4}
=\frac{162}{0.167426856}\approx 967.59
\]

\[
\boxed{967.59}
\]
